format: y/YYYY.bin.gz = gzip of little-endian: char[4] "UD01", u16 nT, u16 nD, u16 tickerIdx[nT], u16 dayIdx[nD], u16 p[nD][nT] (p_up*10000, 65535=missing), i16 r[nD][nT] (o2c return in bp, -32768=missing)
notes: Research page, not a trading signal.

Model updown_o2c_v2. It replaces updown_o2c_v1 after a leak audit (see LEAK_AUDIT.md in this folder). v1 used the split-adjusted price LEVEL, both as a feature and in the $1 universe filter. Yahoo adjusts past prices for later splits, so that level leaked which names would later reverse-split. v2 uses only ratios and returns, and its $1 filter uses the actual (unadjusted) prior close.

Every past day is a walk-forward out-of-sample prediction. The model was trained only on dates at least 2 sessions earlier. Features use only Yahoo bars before that day plus that day's official 09:30 open.

Dev period 2020-01-02..2026-07-02, yearly retrain. FINAL HOLDOUT from 2026-07-06, scored once with the frozen v2 model. Honesty note: v1's holdout results had already been seen when the v2 leak fix was made. The fix came from the audit checklist, and nothing was tuned on the holdout.

OPEN-PRICE CAVEAT: the model uses today's official open (the gap), and the same open is the entry price of the open->close target. You cannot know the official open before an opening-auction order is locked in, and after the open you pay the spread again. So the open->close edge shown here cannot be captured as printed. With no same-day open information at all, ranking drops to AUC ~0.52, and the after-fee long-short is negative on dev (-0.20%/day) and not significant on the holdout (+0.07%/day, t 0.6).

SURVIVORSHIP: the stock list is names still trading in 2026. Companies that disappeared in 2018-2025 are missing from the dev period. This cannot be fixed with the available data. The per-year AUC shows no decay toward recent years, and the holdout (almost no survivorship) gives the same AUC.
Prices: Yahoo split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted. Universe: >=60 prior bars, actual prior close >= $1, 20-day mean dollar volume >= $1M.

Call = UP when p_up > 0.5. The base rate is below 50%, so most calls are DOWN. The within-day ranking (decile) is the more useful read. On the holdout the 0/1 hit rate does not beat always-down; AUC, log-loss and the decile spread do beat the baselines.
